name: OKRIN
author: completion-agent (sparse clue + forced completion)
description: Friendship-bracelet completion law. THE OBJECT (what a demo shows): a bead bracelet drawn as a little grid of coloured beads, threads/gaps drawn with . - _ or ~. Beads are the six bead colours R=red O=orange Y=yellow G=green B=blue P=purple; the CLUE is the bracelet's colour order, k distinct bead colours, k in 3..5 (3-5 chars, e.g. 'BRYP'). Everything that is not one of the clue's colours is thread. Three things must hold. (1) SEED / forced completion: the FIRST ROW of the bracelet must begin with the clue's colour order, so the answer completes a fixed start the scorer rebuilds from the clue alone; no clue-independent witness can exist. (2) DIAGONAL STRIPES (local, chiral): for beads that touch side-to-side or top-to-bottom, the bead to the RIGHT is the next colour in the clue's order (wrapping) and the bead BELOW is the previous colour - so each colour runs down-right along a diagonal, exactly the diagonal stripe of a real friendship bracelet. Only touching pairs are checked, so a second strand may start on a different colour. No bead may be alone: every bead touches another bead. (3) RAINBOW COUNT: a colour is used exactly 2 + its RAINBOW rank among the clue's colours times (2..k+1, keyed to rainbow order ROYGBP, NOT to the order the clue names them - the two clauses use two different orderings of the same colours, which is the second independent discovery). Totals: 9/14/20 beads. Intended discovery path: one demo shows the top row spelling the clue and stripes running down-right (a kid reads both off the picture); counting beads gives 2,3,..,k+1 but in a scrambled order until the player sorts the colours by the RAINBOW (a 12-year-old's first guess; an LLM's first guess is alphabetical, which is a different order for this palette and scores 0). Witnesses closed: the clue alone and any single row fail the counts; a scatter of non-touching beads fails the no-lonely-bead clause; a solid rectangle or a full stripe sheet fails the counts; a bracelet built for another clue is all thread; a mirrored/rotated/indented bracelet fails the first-row clause; counts in clue order, in alphabetical order, or with the stripes running the other way all score 0. Clues whose colour order already agrees with the rainbow (1/k! of instances) score 1 under the clue-order count hypothesis - a deliberate partial-credit gradient; alphabetical-order counts coincide with rainbow-order counts for ~14% of clues, a second small gradient that rewards the wrong-but-close LLM prior. Count base 2 keeps every rank profile comfortably weavable (a class-t bead can only touch class t+-1 beads). generate is uniform over k in {3,4,4,5,5} and a random order of k of the six bead colours. VERSION 2 (RE-SKIN, 2026-09-04) of the class measured in sim/results/lab-OKRIN-1 as an abstract letter grid (v1 kept as challenges/lab/OKRIN.v1.json): AI balance was on target there (OKRINa cracked in round 4 after 3 demos, 100% final; OKRINb partial at 73% - it found the counts and the Toeplitz law g[r][c]=clue[(c-r)%n] but never the seed clause and faked it with a width-mod-n lookup table), but the 12-year-old judge scored v1 1.8/5: abstract letters, decoy letters, alphabetical-rank counts, and a nameable 'Toeplitz diagonal grid'. This version keeps every load-bearing mechanic byte-for-byte in structure (seed row from the clue, chiral neighbour law, per-colour count profile keyed to a second ordering) and changes only the skin and the key: letters -> the six bead colours, alphabet rank -> rainbow rank, decoy non-clue letters dropped, and solve() now weaves one tight bracelet (dents filled first, growth hugging the top-left) instead of scattering components across a large sheet, so the first demo is a small striped band a kid can read. The rainbow key is the centaur hook: the kid supplies 'sort them like a rainbow', which is the one step an LLM's priors point away from.
